report:
Reviewed the entire extracted narrow_demands claim and all associated evidence. Requirements are (1) demand follows the narrowest semantic boundary across the pipeline, (2) a requested semantic product demands only its necessary interfaces and metadata, and (3) checking a caller may demand the callee signature but never its body. The architectural-foundations reference supplies rationale; it does not narrow this universal guarantee to a single fixture. All three requirements remain explicitly deferred by the sole implementation association in sage_meta::todo in service_spec.rs: whole-compiler enforcement is unfinished and the checked caller scenario lacks ordinary/receiver boundary coverage. This is a justified TODO, not an implementation approval. The captured architecture guide specifies representative module, signature, and body dependency traces as the verification matrix. The captured Stage 5 plan additionally names cold/warm requests, body/signature edits, controlled forbidden edges, and rejection of unmapped work as prerequisites for broader enforcement.

The complete associated test set contains exactly todo::crates_sage_ir_crate_narrow_demands. Its body contains comments and no assertions. Accordingly it supplies no behavioral proof, and its TODO status is essential. Its comment accurately defers focused required/forbidden traces for module, signature, and body products, including explicit no-callee-body assertions. Prerequisites are complete observation/mapping of ordinary calls and receiver identities and a reviewed representative product-demand matrix; until those exist, passing this placeholder must never be interpreted as proving any of the three guarantees.

Captured architecture_contracts.rs as context for the implementation TODO's specific missing-boundary explanation. Its caller test explicitly expects nonconformance, an undeclared call, and a receiver-identity coverage gap while separately asserting a single body request and distinct caller/callee signature keys; this supports retaining the recorded deferral despite selected positive no-callee-body evidence. Its signature test is a narrow cold/warm example. These unassociated examples are not treated as an implementation or complete test approval for this anchor; no general guarantee or verified helper correctness is inferred from them. There are no ordinary or N/A entries to approve and no hidden behavior attributed to the TODO test. A forbidden dependency in an untested module/product would not be detected by this anchor's current placeholder, which is precisely the acknowledged coverage gap. No newly suspected behavioral defect was established. No source changes or test commands were performed; assessment is source inspection with review start/read commands only. Accept the existing explicit implementation and test deferrals without relabeling them implemented; no edits are needed to preserve their honest scope.
